e08q20.ref: The National Assembly for Wales has 60 Assembly members (AMs), and elections are held every four years using a form of proportional representation.
e08q20.note: Senedd terms have been five years since 2016, and the Senedd Cymru (Members and Elections) Act 2024 raised its size to 96 members from the 2026 election. The handbook, and so the test, says 60 members elected every four years.

e15q23.ref: Wallace and Gromit are animated films. Their creator Nick Park has won four Oscars for his animated films, including three for films featuring Wallace and Gromit.

e15q24.ref: In the UK, violence in the home is a serious crime. Anyone who is violent towards their partner, whether a man or a woman, married or living together, can be prosecuted.

e18q02.text: Which British racing driver is named in the handbook as a recent winner of the Formula 1 World Championship?
e18q02.ref: A number of British Grand Prix drivers have won the Formula 1 World Championship. Recent British winners include Damon Hill, Lewis Hamilton and Jenson Button.

e18q03.ref: In 1810 Sake Dean Mahomet opened the Hindoostane Coffee House in George Street, London. It was the first curry house to open in Britain.

e18q04.text: Damon Hill, Lewis Hamilton and Jenson Button are known for which sport?
e18q04.ref: There is a long history of motor sport in the UK. Recent British Formula 1 World Championship winners include Damon Hill, Lewis Hamilton and Jenson Button.

e18q05.text: What is the limit for the small claims procedure in Northern Ireland and Scotland?
e18q05.ref: The small claims procedure is used for claims of less than £10,000 in England and Wales and £5,000 in Scotland and Northern Ireland.

e18q06.ref: Sir Edward Elgar’s best-known work is probably the Pomp and Circumstance Marches. March No 1 (Land of Hope and Glory) is usually played at the Last Night of the Proms.

e18q07.text: Where does the UK government sit?
e18q07.ref: The UK is governed by the parliament sitting in Westminster.

e18q08.text: During the 18th century, what important role appeared in Parliament?
e18q08.ref: George I relied on his ministers. The most important minister in Parliament became known as the Prime Minister. The first man to be called this was Sir Robert Walpole, Prime Minister from 1721 to 1742.

e18q09.text: Which tribes came to Britain from northern Europe after the Romans left in AD 410?
e18q09.ref: Britain was invaded by tribes from northern Europe: the Jutes, the Angles and the Saxons.

e18q10.ref: Henry Tudor became King Henry VII after the Wars of the Roses and married King Richard’s niece, Elizabeth of York, uniting the Houses of Lancaster and York.

e18q11.ref: Pub quizzes are popular. Pool and darts are traditional pub games.

e18q12.text: In which battle did William, Duke of Normandy, defeat Harold, the Saxon king of England?
e18q12.ref: In 1066, William, Duke of Normandy, defeated Harold, the Saxon king of England, at the Battle of Hastings.

e18q14.text: What was the biggest source of employment in Britain before the 18th century?
e18q14.ref: Before the 18th century, agriculture was the biggest source of employment in Britain.

e18q15.text: Which of the following is an aim of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO)?

options.To regulate international trade and econ: To regulate international trade and economic policies among its members

e18q15.ref: NATO is a group of European and North American countries that have agreed to help each other if they come under attack. It also aims to maintain peace between all of its members.

e18q16.text: What name is used for the bombing campaign in which Germany bombed London and other UK cities at night during the Second World War?
e18q16.ref: The German air force continued bombing London and other British cities at night. This was called the Blitz.

e18q17.text: In Northern Ireland, cases in the Magistrates’ Court are heard by a District Judge who is legally qualified.

e18q18.ref: The Welsh Assembly has the power to make laws for Wales in 20 areas, including education and training and health and social services. Since 2011 it can pass laws on these topics without the agreement of the UK Parliament.

e18q19.text: Arranged marriages, where both parties agree to the marriage, are acceptable in the UK.
e18q19.ref: Arranged marriages, where both parties agree to the marriage, are acceptable in the UK. Forced marriage is a criminal offence.

e18q20.text: Is the Scottish Parliament located in Glasgow?
e18q20.ref: The Scottish Parliament sits in Edinburgh, the capital city of Scotland.

e18q21.text: Do I need a TV licence if I only watch TV on a computer?
e18q21.ref: Everyone in the UK with a TV, computer or other medium which can be used for watching TV must have a television licence.

e18q22.text: Which traditional dish of Northern Ireland is a fried meal of bacon, eggs, sausage, black pudding, white pudding, tomatoes, mushrooms, soda bread and potato bread?
e18q22.ref: Northern Ireland: Ulster fry – a fried meal with bacon, eggs, sausage, black pudding, white pudding, tomatoes, mushrooms, soda bread and potato bread.

e18q23.text: What are the British scientists Sir Ian Wilmot and Keith Campbell famous for?

Cloning a mammal, Dolly the sheep.

e18q23.ref: In 1996, Sir Ian Wilmot and Keith Campbell led a team which was the first to succeed in cloning a mammal, Dolly the sheep.

e18q24.ref: 1 March: St David’s Day (Wales); 17 March: St Patrick’s Day (Northern Ireland); 23 April: St George’s Day (England); 30 November: St Andrew’s Day (Scotland).

e18q25.text: Which TWO of these are long-running British soap operas?
e18q25.ref: British television shows a wide variety of programmes. Popular programmes include regular soap operas such as Coronation Street and EastEnders.

e18q26.text: Under whose reign did the 13 North American colonies declare their independence in 1776?
e18q26.ref: In 1776, 13 American colonies declared their independence, stating that people had a right to establish their own governments. The king at the time was George III.

e18q27.text: Are members of the Scottish Parliament (MSPs) elected by a form of proportional representation?
e18q27.ref: The Scottish Parliament has 129 members (MSPs), elected by a form of proportional representation.

e18q13.ref: The Turing Award is the leading award in computer science. The handbook does not mention the award itself, but it does describe Alan Turing, whose theoretical ‘Turing machine’ was influential in the development of the modern-day computer.
